paragraphs: Pappos ben Yehudah. A great sage in a baraita, and through him things went well for Israel. In Helek there are two expositions in his name. At the end of Berakhot, 61b, he was arrested after R' Akiva was arrested and said to R' Akiva, ‘Happy are you, who were arrested over words of Torah,’ etc. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Ha-Sefinah, Rabban Gamliel and R' Yehoshua saw him. Rabban Gamliel asked R' Yehoshua, ‘Who is this?’ He answered, ‘Pappos ben Yehudah, all of whose deeds are for the sake of Heaven.’ But this attestation is false [the target of the criticism is not explicit], for there the text says ‘Yehudah ben Pappos’ (see there). In Sifra, Behukkotai, ‘I shall break the pride of your strength’: Israel's pride, such as Pappos ben Yehudah and Lulinos Alexandri. In Yalkut there: ‘and Alexandri.’
